Introduction

A Licensed Home Care Services Agency (LHCSA) in New York provides non-medical personal care and home health aide services. The NY State Department of Health oversees LHCSA licensing under Public Health Law Article 36.

Table of Contents

  • Understand New York’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand New York’s Regulations

NY DOH licenses LHCSAs under strict regulations including 10 NYCRR Part 766. Requirements include character and competence review, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

LHCSAs provide personal care, home health aide services, homemaker, and companion services. New York’s large managed care market creates significant volume opportunities.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the NY DOS, apply for LHCSA license, undergo character and competence review, and secure required insurance and bonding.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

New York benchmarks: Private pay rates $25-$40/hour, Medicaid managed care rates $20-$30/hour, break-even 12-24 months. NYC and surrounding areas have highest demand.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office meeting DOH requirements, implement scheduling and EVV systems, and establish quality monitoring.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

NY requires extensive background checks and DOH-approved training for all aides.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop comprehensive policies meeting DOH regulatory requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build relationships with managed care organizations, hospitals, and community organizations.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing, comply with EVV requirements, and prepare for DOH surveys.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does LHCSA licensing take? The process can take 6-12 months due to the character and competence review.
